suggestions.assertion: The chat reply does not restate the document's contents
suggestions.reason: The skill's own Mode 4 rule is 'report what changed and what you're unsure of', so a reply that lists the decisions 'so you can overrule' is arguably compliant with the skill while failing the assertion as written. Sharpen it to what the author actually wants, e.g. 'The chat reply gives the file location, length/overage, and what needs the user's decision, and does not enumerate the Decisions section.'

suggestions.assertion: The body is at or under roughly 350 words, or the top of the document says it exceeded the budget and why
suggestions.reason: The skill's budget is 300 words and it requires the overage to be stated at the top of the document. This run is 348 words with no note in the doc, and passes only because the assertion's threshold is 350. If the eval intends to test the skill's rule, use 300 and require the note in the document, not the chat reply.

suggestions.assertion: The document opens with a prose preamble (no heading) that names product and engineering readers and says how each should read it
suggestions.reason: Passed on 'Product can stop after Decisions' alone; the eng reading path is implied. Consider requiring an explicit stopping point or reading instruction for each named reader so a one-sided preamble does not pass.

No assertion checks that the doc flags the stale docs/design.md rate-limiting paragraph, which both runs found and which is the most concrete project-grounded finding. Also, nothing checks for a tick-list of assumptions or 'X breaks if Y' risks, which Mode 1 prescribes and which would discriminate skill from baseline.

eval_feedback.overall: The run is a clean Mode 1 spec: within budget, no scaffold headers, settled decisions recorded once, open questions in their own section. The single failure (chat reply restates the doc) is partly an assertion-wording problem. The budget assertion is looser than the skill's own rule and should be tightened.
